question: A UPS acceptance test includes:
choices: Static transfer from inverter to bypass and back
A vacuum-bottle pressure test
Tan delta of the battery jars only
Table 100.6 cable VLF in place of a function test
explanation: ATS 7.22.2 calls for the static transfer both ways, on normal load when you can. The pass criterion is the manufacturer’s data for that transfer, not a cable table.

question: Automatic transfer switch control wiring shall not be less than:
choices: 2 MΩ
100 MΩ at 5 kV
The generator’s PI
explanation: 7.22.3.D.3 is 2 MΩ on control wiring. Power-contact microhms are a different line. The generator’s polarization index does not grade the transfer-switch wiring.

question: An automatic transfer switch test is not finished when the relay picks up. ATS 7.22.3 also wants you to time:
choices: Delay on transfer, and delay plus retransfer when normal returns
Only the generator oil pressure
The fiber attenuation
The station battery specific gravity
explanation: The section lists time delay on transfer, the transfer itself, and time delay and retransfer when normal power returns. A contact closure in the test set does not prove the switch moved and came back.

question: During a UPS static-transfer test the inverter is the source and bypass is healthy. The test should show:
choices: Transfer to bypass and back, within the manufacturer’s time
That the bypass breaker is welded shut
A recloser vacuum test
Tan delta of the output cable instead of a transfer
explanation: ATS 7.22.2 wants the transfer both directions, preferably on real load, and the result compared with the UPS manual. A single transfer that never returns does not finish the test.

question: A step-up transformer can be back-fed from the low-voltage side. Before a power-factor test you:
choices: Assume the LV bushings are dead because the HV breaker is open
Isolate and test both sides, because the LV side may be the source
Only ground the HV neutral
Skip LOTO if the nameplate says distribution
explanation: Opening the high side does not kill a unit fed from inverters, a generator, or another LV source. 29 CFR 1910.333 still wants every source disconnected, locked, and tested. Then the test voltage stays within the winding’s line-to-ground rating.
reference: 29 CFR 1910.333(b)(2); power-factor method, per Megger DELTA4000 applications guide

question: ATS 7.22.1.B.3 on an engine generator requires verification of:
choices: Phase rotation, phasing, and synchronized operation as the application requires
Only the oil dielectric strength
Zone 1 reach
A 30-minute VLF test of the stator
explanation: The generator has to land on the bus in the right rotation and in phase when the application needs that. The insulation-resistance test is a separate item, run in accordance with IEEE 43.

question: ATS 7.22.1.B.6 calls for the engine-generator performance test to be run:
choices: In accordance with NFPA 110
As a 30-minute VLF test
Only if the polarization index fails
In place of the protective-shutdown tests
explanation: The performance test follows NFPA 110. The insulation-resistance test and the protective-shutdown tests are separate lines in the same section. Do not replace those with the performance run, or the other way around.

question: NFPA 70B-2026 says maintenance information designates equipment as:
choices: Serviceable, limited-service, or nonserviceable
Pass, fail, or exempt from records
Class 1, 1A, or 2 only
Condition A or B
explanation: Those three words say what the equipment can still be used for. They are not the same as the condition score of 1, 2, or 3 that sets how often it is maintained.

question: NFPA 70B-2026 chapter 32 applies to a battery energy storage system above:
choices: 3.6 MJ, which is 1 kWh
50 kWh only
Any single flooded cell
A transfer switch
explanation: The storage-system chapter starts above 3.6 MJ, equal to 1 kWh. That energy number does not by itself pull every standby battery into the chapter. Section 32.1.2 lists the applications that stay outside it. When the manufacturer is silent, performance for a system that is in the chapter follows that chapter's interval table.

question: Which test is on the battery-energy-storage list in NFPA 70B-2026 Table 32.3.5 and would be the wrong list for a standby battery jar?
choices: Battery-management-system review, thermal survey, and ultrasonic inspection
Specific gravity of a flooded cell
Individual float voltage to two decimals
Connection resistance of a vented cell
explanation: The storage-system table includes a thermal survey, ultrasonic inspection, cable insulation resistance, connection resistance, a performance test, and a review of the battery-management system. Specific gravity and two-decimal float voltage are the stationary-standby chapter. A system at or below 1 kWh is not pulled into chapter 32 by the title alone.

question: NFPA 70B-2026 visual inspection of a transfer switch, conditions 1, 2, and 3, is:
choices: 12, 6, and 3 months
60, 36, and 12 months, the same as the electrical row
12, 12, and 6 months, the transformer-fluid row
Before each use
explanation: Visual inspection of transfer switches is 12, 6, and 3 months. The other transfer-switch tasks, when the manufacturer is silent, are 60, 36, and 12 months. Do not put the visual check on the grounding electrical-test row.

question: Which test is listed for a transfer switch in NFPA 70B-2026 Table 39.3.5?
choices: Insulation resistance, protective devices, operators, transfer sequence, bypass or isolation, and operation under load
Dissolved-gas analysis
Vacuum-interrupter integrity
A turns-ratio test of the switch
explanation: The transfer-switch electrical list is insulation resistance, protective devices, the operators, the transfer sequence, bypass or isolation when the switch has it, and operation under load. Oil tests and vacuum-bottle tests belong to other equipment. No transfer-time limit is printed.

question: A test that is NOT part of caring for a transfer switch under NFPA 70B-2026 Table 39.3.5 is:
choices: Operating the transfer under load
Proving the bypass or isolation mechanism when the switch has one
Functional transfer testing
A dissolved-gas analysis of the switch
explanation: The electrical list includes insulation resistance, protective devices, operators, functional transfer testing, bypass or isolation, and operation under load. Dissolved gas is a liquid-filled transformer test, not a transfer-switch test.

question: When the manufacturer is silent, NFPA 70B-2026 Table 32.2 puts battery-energy-storage performance, conditions 1, 2, and 3, at:
choices: 36, 36, and 12 months
12, 12, and 1 month, the vented float-voltage row
24, 24, and 12 months, the valve-regulated cell performance row
Before each use
explanation: That performance row is for a storage system above 1 kWh. It is not the stationary-standby float-voltage interval and it is not the valve-regulated jar performance row. The storage tests are thermal, ultrasonic, cable insulation, connection resistance, performance, and a battery-management review. No kilowatt-hour pass limit is printed beyond the chapter threshold.

question: Servicing a transfer switch under NFPA 70B-2026 includes manual operation, bolted connections, and interlocks. Those are not the same item as:
choices: The electrical list of insulation resistance, operators, sequence, and operation under load
A job you may skip if the visual interval has not come due
Something the chapter assigns to a relay timing test
A dissolved-gas sample
explanation: Manual operation, bolted connections, and interlocks are the servicing checks. The electrical table then calls for insulation resistance, protective devices, operators, the transfer sequence, bypass or isolation, and operation under load. Visual inspection is still 12, 6, and 3 months. No operating-time limit is printed.

question: Which engine shutdowns does ATS 7.22.1 have you functionally test on a generator set?
choices: Low fuel tank level, ambient temperature, and humidity
Low oil pressure, overtemperature, and overspeed
Battery charger ripple and dc ground
Exhaust stack height and muffler noise
explanation: The safety shutdowns that protect the engine are proved by actually operating them: low oil pressure, overtemperature, and overspeed. Source: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 7.22.1.B.4.

question: During inspection of an automatic transfer switch, ATS 7.22.3 has you check manual transfer and also:
choices: That both sources can be closed together briefly to share load
That the neutral is bonded at the switch
That the generator is synchronized before each transfer
Positive mechanical interlocking between sources
explanation: The mechanical interlock must keep the two sources from being connected together. Manual transfer is checked along with it. Source: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 7.22.3.A.9 and A.10.

question: On a UPS acceptance test, ATS 7.22.2 checks the dc undervoltage setting. When the dc falls to that level it should:
choices: Start the standby generator
Transfer the load to the maintenance bypass manually
Raise the charger to equalize voltage
Trip the inverter input breaker
explanation: The dc undervoltage trip protects the battery and inverter by opening the inverter input breaker. The level is set to the manufacturer's value. Source: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 7.22.2.B.4 and D.4.

question: The normal source to an automatic transfer switch fails. In what order should the ATS operate? (ATS 7.22.3 has you verify each of these functions.)
choices: Transfer, engine start, alternate source sensed, delay on transfer
Normal sensing drops, engine starts, alternate sensed, delay, transfer
Engine start, transfer, normal-source sensing drops out, delay on transfer
Delay on retransfer, engine start, transfer, alternate sensed
explanation: ATS lists normal-source voltage and frequency sensing, engine start, time delay on transfer, alternate-source sensing, transfer, and then delay with retransfer and engine cooldown and shutdown when normal returns. That is a checklist, not the running order. In operation the transfer delay only finishes and the switch only moves once the alternate source is up and sensed good. Source: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 7.22.3.B.8.

question: Utility power returns after an outage. In the ATS 7.22.3 timing list, what follows the retransfer?
choices: An immediate engine stop at the instant of retransfer
Engine cooldown, then shutdown
A second transfer back to the generator
A battery equalize charge
explanation: After the retransfer delay and the retransfer, the engine runs unloaded for its cooldown period and then shuts down. Both times are verified. Source: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 7.22.3.B.8.

question: A 125 kW standby generator stator gives a 1-minute insulation test with a dielectric absorption ratio of 1.2. Under ATS 7.22.1:
choices: It fails, because the DAR must be at least 1.4
It needs a 10-minute PI test because of its size
It fails, because every generator must show a PI of 2.0 from a 1-minute test
It meets the DAR limit (above 1.0); check Table 100.11 too
explanation: Machines of 200 hp (150 kW) and below get a 1-minute test and a DAR, which must be greater than 1.0. Larger machines get a 10-minute test and a PI of at least 2.0. The 1.4 DAR figure is for induction motors under 7.15.1. Source: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025 7.22.1.B.1 and D.1.

question: Emergency loads hang on a single feeder through one automatic transfer switch. What does NEC 700.5 add so the switch can be maintained?
choices: Nothing; the switch is taken out of service for maintenance
A second utility service only
A portable generator connection in place of the transfer switch
Redundant transfer equipment or a bypass-isolation switch
explanation: 700.5(D) asks for redundant transfer equipment or a bypass-isolation switch when emergency loads are on a single feeder, so 700.3(C) maintenance can be done without losing the loads. 700.5(B) says bypass-isolation switches must prevent inadvertent paralleling. If the backup path is manual, a qualified person actively supervises it while the automatic switch is out. Source: NFPA 70-2023 (NEC), 700.5(B) and (D).

question: Where does ATS 7.22.3 direct insulation-resistance testing of a transfer switch?
choices: Every pole with the switch in each source position, plus across open poles
Phase-to-ground only, with the switch in the normal position
Only across the closed contacts
Control wiring only, at 2,500 V dc
explanation: B.2 covers both source positions and across each open pole. Control wiring is a separate item at 500 V dc for 300 V cable or 1,000 V dc for 600 V cable, with 2 MΩ minimum. Source: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025, 7.22.3.B.2, B.3 and D.3.

question: Contact resistance across the poles of a transfer switch reads 42, 45 and 66 µΩ. With no manufacturer's range, what does ATS say?
choices: Accept all three: they are under 100 µΩ
Investigate the 45 µΩ pole, since it differs from the 42 µΩ pole
Investigate the 66 µΩ pole: it is more than 50% above the lowest value
Investigate only if a pole exceeds twice the average
explanation: Without manufacturer data, ATS compares poles and flags any that deviate by more than 50% of the lowest. 42 × 1.5 = 63 µΩ, so 66 µΩ is over and 45 µΩ is not. Source: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025, 7.22.3.B.4 and D.4.

question: How does NEC 700.5(C) require an automatic transfer switch for an emergency system to be operated and held?
choices: Manually operated and electrically held
Electrically operated and electrically held
Electrically operated and mechanically held
Spring operated with no holding means
explanation: An emergency ATS must be electrically operated and mechanically held. The holding is mechanical, not dependent on a coil staying energized. Source: NFPA 70-2023 (NEC), 700.5(C).

question: Under the NEC, an emergency-system transfer switch must be:
choices: Automatic, listed for emergency use, and unable to interconnect the sources
Manual, so a qualified person on site decides every single transfer
Shared with standby loads so the generator stays loaded
Reconditioned equipment, if it passes a functional test
explanation: 700.5 requires automatic, listed, emergency-marked transfer equipment that cannot interconnect the sources by accident. It supplies only emergency loads. Reconditioned transfer switches are not allowed. Source: NFPA 70-2023 (NEC), 700.5(A) and (E); 700.2.

question: Under NEC 700.12, how quickly must an emergency system supply power after normal power fails?
choices: Within 60 seconds
Within 5 minutes, measured from the generator reaching rated speed
There is no time limit; it depends only on the generator
Within the time required for the application, but not more than 10 seconds
explanation: 700.12 caps emergency systems at 10 seconds. Legally required standby under 701.12 gets 60 seconds. The project specification can be stricter, so check it too. Source: NFPA 70-2023 (NEC), 700.12 and 701.12.

question: Normal power comes back for only a moment during a test, and the emergency transfer switch should not run straight back to normal. Which NEC feature is that?
choices: An in-phase monitor on the alternate source
A time delay that rides through a brief return of normal power
An elevator pre-signal contact that warns the elevator controller
A load-shed contact that drops nonessential loads
explanation: 700.12 calls for a time delay so that a short return of normal power does not cause a retransfer. ATS 7.22.3 has you time the retransfer delay against the design during the functional test. Source: NFPA 70-2023 (NEC), 700.12(D)(1); ANSI/NETA ATS-2025, 7.22.3.B.8.

question: Who witnesses the commissioning test of an NEC Article 700 emergency system, and what must be kept afterward?
choices: The generator vendor only, with no written record required
The AHJ witnesses it, and a written test and maintenance record is kept
The serving utility, which keeps the records in its own files
The electrical inspector only if a failure occurs
explanation: 700.3 has the AHJ witness the test on installation and periodically, sets periodic tests on an approved schedule, requires maintenance, and requires a written record of tests and maintenance. Source: NFPA 70-2023 (NEC), 700.3(A)-(D).

question: On a transfer switch functional test, the engine-start, transfer, retransfer and cooldown delays all operate. How do you judge the measured times?
choices: Against a fixed NETA table of seconds for each delay
Against the previous technician's notes only
Any time under 60 seconds passes for every delay in the sequence
Against the manufacturer's data and the system design settings
explanation: ATS 7.22.3.D.8 sends you to the manufacturer and the system design. It has no fixed table of seconds. Record each setting and each measured time so the next test can compare. Source: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025, 7.22.3.D.8.

question: Besides the timing list, which two electrical items does ATS 7.22.3 add for a transfer switch's controls and sources?
choices: Relays and timers set per Section 7.9, and phase rotation and phasing verified
Measure turns ratio and excitation current on the switch's control transformer
Run a VLF withstand on the load cables in both source positions
Perform a dissolved-gas analysis of the switch
explanation: B.6 sends relays and timers to Section 7.9. B.7 checks that both sources have matching rotation and phasing, plus synchronized operation where the application uses it. Source: ANSI/NETA ATS-2025, 7.22.3.B.6 and B.7.
